milestones.note: On April 27, 2026 the developers announced the gas turbines and diesel generators would be replaced by Bloom Energy fuel cells.

Status.note:
This confirms the cancelled status as a gas plant, so it is not a change.

The cancellation:
- An Oracle press release from April 27, 2026 at https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/oracle-borderplex-and-bloom-energy-to-power-project-jupiter-with-fuel-cell-technology-2026-04-27/ says the updated power design 'will replace Project Jupiter's previously planned gas turbines and diesel generators'.
- A Source NM article from April 27, 2026 at https://sourcenm.com/2026/04/27/nm-project-jupiter-data-center-developers-announce-new-plans-for-generating-power/ says the same in its first paragraph. The two are separate publishers.
- The New Mexico Environment Department record lists the East and West microgrid applications 10732 and 10734 as 'Application Withdrawn 4/27/2026' (permit harvest file scopes/us-nm/work/permits/L100001080450.md). That gives the dated step.

Backup Power.note:
This is the permit that now covers the site, Yucca Growth Infrastructure application 10883, and it allows no backup engines.

Where to find it:
- Open the draft Statement of Basis from July 29, 2026 at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/NmE1OTcwZDc1NzQ2NGE2YjU1MWNiODEzZl8yMzYxNzc~.pdf. Under the section on emergency and backup power it says 'Fuel Cells Modules are the only equipment authorized at the facility to provide power ... and to provide all backup power during load spikes' and that generators 'are not allowed'.
- The same document says no stationary spark ignition or diesel engines are at the facility.
- The draft permit Part A at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/OTRmYzlmMmMwMTljZDUyM2VkM2I5Y2ZkY18yMzYxNzM~.pdf limits the plant to 2,462 MW of Bloom fuel cells.

So Backup Power stays no. There is no backup engine fleet to add as a new plant.

qa.question: Should the 2026 start year on cancelled unit East be cleared?
qa.finding: The unit is cancelled and still carries a start year of 2026. The manual says cancelled units never carry a start year. The cancellation holds, as the Oracle press release at https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/oracle-borderplex-and-bloom-energy-to-power-project-jupiter-with-fuel-cell-technology-2026-04-27/ and the Source NM article at https://sourcenm.com/2026/04/27/nm-project-jupiter-data-center-developers-announce-new-plans-for-generating-power/ both say the gas turbines were replaced on April 27, 2026.
qa.recommendation: Clear the Start year on the East unit in the web form and leave Cancellation year as 2026.
qa.note: The start year's existing source is the 2025 air permit file, which described the gas turbine plan that was withdrawn.

qa.question: Is the EIP facility YGI Microgrid the same project as this plant?
qa.finding: EIP Oil and Gas Watch lists a facility called YGI Microgrid, proposed, 2,462 MW, at https://oilandgaswatch.org/facility/107ebccf-3e9e-48b1-a8d6-d5a09af92d7a. New Mexico air permit 10883 is for the Yucca Growth Infrastructure 'YGI Microgrid' and its draft permit Part A at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/OTRmYzlmMmMwMTljZDUyM2VkM2I5Y2ZkY18yMzYxNzM~.pdf names 2,462 MW of Bloom fuel cells, so the figure matches the fuel cell redesign of Project Jupiter.
qa.recommendation: Treat YGI Microgrid as the fuel cell version of this plant and add no new plant, since the tracker does not cover gas fuel cells. Add the EIP facility id 107ebccf-3e9e-48b1-a8d6-d5a09af92d7a to Other IDs (location).
qa.note: The EIP page did not load with the text 'YGI' in the verification run, so the link was not verified. The match rests on the permit number, the name and the 2,462 MW figure.

qa.question: Does the permit show a different size from the 2,210 MW in GEM?
qa.finding: The draft permit Part A at https://cloud.env.nm.gov/resources/_translator.php/OTRmYzlmMmMwMTljZDUyM2VkM2I5Y2ZkY18yMzYxNzM~.pdf says a maximum of 2,275 fuel cell clusters with 2,462 MW. GEM's 2,210 MW (1,223 plus 987) comes from the earlier gas turbine applications.
qa.recommendation: Leave the capacity at 2,210 MW, because the plant stays cancelled as a gas turbine plant and the tracker does not cover fuel cells.
qa.note: No change is proposed. Backup engines at 50 MW summed were not found: the permit allows none.
